title: Ving Tsun Kwoon Vocabulary
publisher: Shun Mo Scientific Ving Tsun (WSL lineage)
verifyNote: Cantonese terms compiled from public glossaries (CantoDict, Wiktionary, Wikipedia glossary of Wing Chun terms) and cross-checked; NOT confirmed against the school's own materials. Character choices flagged in docs/wing-chun-study-path.md §2 need a Sifu's confirmation. word fields use traditional (繁) characters; pinyin fields are Mandarin (reference only); dojo pronunciation is Cantonese, carried in the gloss.

lessons.title: 師父同武館
lessons.topic: The people in a kwoon and what you call them

words.gloss: Sifu (si1 fu6) — your own teacher, 'teacher-father'
Sihing (si1 hing1) — senior kung-fu brother
Sidai (si1 dai6) — junior kung-fu brother
Sije (si1 ze2) — senior kung-fu sister
Simui (si1 mui6) — junior kung-fu sister
Sigung (si1 gung1) — your Sifu's Sifu, 'grand-teacher'
To Dai (tou4 dai6) — disciple / student
Kwoon (mou5 gun2) — the martial-arts hall

lessons.title: 詠春同禮節
lessons.topic: Naming the art you practise and how you bow in

words.gloss: Ving Tsun (wing6 ceon1) — 'praising spring,' the art itself
Kung Fu (gung1 fu1) — 'skill from effort,' martial arts generally
Kuen (kyun4) — fist / boxing / style (as in 詠春拳)
Tou Lou (tou3 lou6) — 'form / routine,' a solo set
Dui Chaak (deoi3 caak3) — 'paired dismantling,' partner application drills
Bai Si (baai3 si1) — 'to bow to a master,' the discipleship ceremony
Bao Kuen Lai (pou5 kyun4 lai5) — 'fist-wrapping salute,' palm over fist
Ma Bou (maa5 bou6) — 'horse stance,' stance generically

lessons.title: 拳套同兵器
lessons.topic: The named curriculum you progress through

words.gloss: Siu Nim Tau (siu2 nim6 tau4) — 'little idea,' 1st form, structure & centerline
Chum Kiu (cam4 kiu4) — 'seeking the bridge,' 2nd form, turning & stepping
Biu Jee (biu1 zi2) — 'thrusting fingers,' 3rd form, recovery & emergency
Muk Yan Jong (muk6 jan4 zong1) — 'wooden man post,' the dummy
Baat Cham Dao (baat3 zaam2 dou1) — 'eight-slashing knives,' butterfly swords
Luk Dim Boon Kwun (luk6 dim2 bun3 gwan3) — 'six-and-a-half point pole,' the long pole

lessons.title: 碌手基本手法
lessons.titlePinyin: luk1 sau2 gei1 bun2 sau2 faat3
lessons.topic: Tan / Bong / Fook plus Wu / Pak / Man — the first drills

words.gloss: Tan Sau (taan1 sau2) — 'spreading hand,' palm-up receiving arm
Bong Sau (bong2 sau2) — 'wing arm,' elbow-up deflection / recovery
Fook Sau (fuk6 sau2) — 'subduing hand,' bridging-on-top control
Wu Sau (wu6 sau2) — 'guarding hand,' rear centerline guard
Pak Sau (paak3 sau2) — 'slapping hand,' lateral clear
Man Sau (man6 sau2) — 'asking hand,' lead seeking hand

lessons.title: 更多手法
lessons.topic: The second wave of hand techniques (手法)

words.gloss: Lap Sau (laap3 sau2) — 'grabbing/pulling hand,' jerking pull (char flag §2)
Jut Sau (zat6 sau2) — 'jerking hand,' short shocking snap
Huen Sau (hyun1 sau2) — 'circling hand,' wrist circle to change line
Jum Sau (zam2 sau2) — 'sinking hand,' downward forearm pressure
Gaan Sau (gaang1 sau2) — 'ploughing hand,' diagonal splitting block
Laan Sau (laan4 sau2) — 'barring hand,' horizontal forearm bar
Kwan Sau (kwan2 sau2) — 'binding hand,' combined bong+tan rotation

lessons.title: 撳割掌法
lessons.topic: Pinning and cutting hands, the elbow, and palm strikes

words.gloss: Gum Sau (gam6 sau2) — 'pressing hand,' flat downward pin (char flag §2)
Yan Sau (jan3 sau2) — 'stamping hand,' sealing/pinning press
Got Sau (got3 sau2) — 'cutting hand,' slicing deflection
Jarn (zaang1) — 'elbow' (char flag §2); strikes: 批踭 pai jarn, 跪踭 gwai jarn
Jeung (zoeng2) — 'palm,' generic palm strike
Jing Jeung (jing3 zoeng2) — 'front palm,' forward palm on centerline
Wang Jeung (waang4 zoeng2) — 'side palm,' lateral palm
Dai Jeung (dai2 zoeng2) — 'bottom palm,' upward heel-of-palm
Yat Ji Chung Kuen (jat6 zi6 cung1 kyun4) — 'sun-character thrust punch,' the vertical punch
Lin Wan Kuen (lin4 waan4 kyun4) — 'linked fists,' chain punching
Jik Tek (zik6 tek3) — 'straight kick,' front thrusting kick
Wang Tek (waang4 tek3) — 'horizontal kick,' side/stamping kick
Mai Jarn (maai4 zaang1) — 'closing the elbow,' WSL elbow-to-centerline theory
Tan Da (taan1 daa2) — 'tan + strike,' simultaneous defend-and-punch
Bong Da (bong2 daa2) — 'bong + strike,' simultaneous defend-and-strike

lessons.title: 馬步同步法
lessons.topic: The stance and how you move it (馬步)

words.gloss: Yee Jee Kim Yeung Ma (ji6 zi6 kim4 joeng4 maa5) — 'char-2 goat-clamping stance,' the basic stance
Biu Ma (biu1 maa5) — 'thrusting stance,' driving shuffle-step
Huen Ma (hyun1 maa5) — 'circling step,' angle-changing footwork
Juen Ma (zyun3 maa5) — 'turning stance,' the heel pivot (Chum Kiu)
Seung Ma (soeng5 maa5) — 'advancing stance,' step in
Tui Ma (teoi3 maa5) — 'retreating stance,' step back (char flag §2)

lessons.title: 黐手家族
lessons.topic: The sticking-hands progression up to free rolling

words.gloss: Chi Sau (ci1 sau2) — 'sticking hands,' the sensitivity drill
Daan Chi Sau (daan1 ci1 sau2) — 'single sticking hand'
Seung Chi Sau (soeng1 ci1 sau2) — 'double sticking hand'
Luk Sau (luk1 sau2) — 'rolling arms,' the rolling drill (also 盤手 poon sau)
Gor Sau (gwo3 sau2) — 'crossing hands,' free rolling beyond fixed chi-sau
Lat Sau (lat1 sau2) — 'freed hand,' contact lost (Canto/Mand differ, §0)

lessons.title: 理念同心法
lessons.topic: The theory that ties it all together

words.gloss: Chung Sin (zung1 sin3) — 'centerline,' prime target & defense line
Ji Ng Sin (zi2 ng5 sin3) — 'meridian axis,' the central vertical axis
Chiu Min Jeui Ying (ciu4 min6 zeoi1 jing4) — 'face the foe, chase the form'
Loi Lau Hui Sung (loi4 lau4 heoi3 sung3) — 'what comes, retain; what leaves, send off'
Lat Sau Jik Chung (lat1 sau2 zik6 cung1) — 'hand freed → thrust straight in'
Chun Ging (cyun3 ging6) — 'inch power,' short-range explosive force
Je Lik (ze3 lik6) — 'borrowing force,' use the opponent's own force
